Record 2020 despite COVID disruption: FY revenue over $130M, ~$8.5M income, ~$15M EBITDA; Q4 revenue +48% to $35.7M (domestic +67%).
North American distribution expansion the primary driver - DSD network now 150+ partners covering ~85% of major metro markets, total US doors above 82,000.
Explosive e-commerce momentum - Celsius reached the third-largest energy brand on Amazon at 14.5% share (Amazon sales +224.8%).
Record Q4 gross margin of 48.9% (+700 bps) aided by lower promotions, stronger euro and supply-chain synergies - management explicitly cautioned these may not transfer to future periods.
Industry-wide aluminum can shortage expected to pressure 2021 gross margin to a 'low 40%' range; Celsius navigated by leveraging Europe/Asia operations to secure cans.
New Speedway account adds ~2,700 locations; 82% of Target now on DSD; CVS/Walmart transitions underway; 7-Eleven DSD conversion planned ~May 2021.
National DSD network now complete - positioned to capture share rapidly into delayed spring planogram resets and the peak summer season.
COVID materially disrupted health/fitness, vending, food-service and international channels - international revenue up only 3%.
FAST protein-snack supply constrained in Finland (confectionery-manufacturer capacity limits/out-of-stocks); Func Food fully integrated and accretive.
Cooler program showing strong economics: ~3-month payback, 200%+ velocity uplift, 1,000+ on order with potential to double by year-end 2021.
Company now debt-free after repaying ~$10M of European acquisition bonds in October 2020; ended 2020 with $43.2M cash.
Adding flavors is incremental and does not cannibalize - lifts the whole portfolio at an increasing rate.
Management emphatically bullish - called 2020 'only the beginning'; teased major summer 2021 marketing/launch plans.
Whether Nielsen data shows acceleration into early 2021 and any sell-in vs sell-through mismatch relative to Q4.
Nielsen extremely strong (~80-90% growth on 2- and 4-week reads for Q1); acknowledged lags between scan data and sell-in timing; North America growth consistent at ~66% in Q4.
Resets delayed due to COVID happening in spring and their impact heading into the peak summer period.

~18,000 doors added in 2020 despite reset delays; spring resets (concentrated in convenience) expected over the next several months, driving a sizable store-count increase, with new distribution also coming on board.
More color on flipping to DSD in the near term/first half where not yet fully converted.

Fully committed to DSD - increased velocity, in-stock improvement, secondary displays. CVS expansion started; more markets transitioning after NYC Big Geyser success. 7-Eleven a major 2021 initiative, transitioning ~May zone by zone (West then East).
Confirm the 200% increase seen with cooler placements.
Confirmed ~200 coolers placed, 1,000+ on order, ~3-month payback, 200%+ velocity increases - some stores becoming the number-one selling energy drink with the right placement.
A year after the Func acquisition, whether management could break out organic growth metrics.

Q4 2019 reflected only two months of consolidated Func revenue vs three months in Q4 2020 - 'apples-and-oranges.' FAST protein-snack portfolio hit by Finland confectionery-manufacturer capacity limits/out-of-stocks; optimistic on European improvement through 2021.
Color on the Strawberry Guava launch and on-the-go Sticks portfolio growth.

Strawberry Guava one of the most successful fitness-channel launches and a fast Amazon turner. On-the-go Sticks growing - now at Walmart, Amazon, Vitamin Shoppe, Publix (chainwide Southeast) - though cans/RTD remain the bulk of revenue.
Q4 margins exceptionally strong but management cautious - what to read into it for 2021 modeling given eight active co-packers.
Confirmed caution - euro pulling back, rising can/sourcing costs, short-term downward pressure on margins, while holding can inventory and managing currency. Flagged Q1 and Q2 specifically.
Which countries saw the most COVID impact and whether international growth bounces back in Q1 or takes a few quarters.

Nordic impact (Sweden potentially closing again, Finland closures) - Q1 could see another impact, but underlying business healthy. Expansion opportunities in UK, Germany, Russia; rapid vaccine rollout aiding government confidence; Nordic Q4 seasonally low.
When Func Food closed, since Q1 2021 becomes apples-to-apples.
Closed October 25, 2019; Q4 2019 reflected ~two months versus three months in Q4 2020; Func was still not fully operational and lacked inventory in late 2019.
Total cost expected for rolling out 1,000 coolers.
Declined to disclose cost but called it a positive-ROI opportunity given high velocity; 1,000 initially on order with potential to double by year-end 2021 as discussions with key accounts progress.
Whether Celsius is in all ~2,700 Speedway locations and whether there is further expansion.
Confirmed ~2,700 Speedway locations with ~2 flavors, with opportunity to add flavors at the next cut-in; drew analogy to 7-Eleven's YoY growth - Speedway locations in good markets.
Reset timing at Target/Walmart and whether near-term SKU expansion is expected.

Spring resets historically run ~March 15-April 15 (convenience can push into May due to COVID); resets expected over coming months with additional flavors on shelf. Adding flavors is incremental, does not cannibalize - lifts the whole portfolio.
Beyond cooler spend, what other marketing programs (sampling, events, Olympics) Celsius is investing in.
'Big things planned' for summer 2021 and great summer launch plans, with a variety of marketing vehicles management declined to detail, focused on increasing household penetration and brand-building.
